title: Pydantic schema validation for NLP tool arguments replacing raw json.loads
context: Tool argument parsing at `_execute_tool_call` used untrusted `json.loads` with no structural or type validation, exposing the agent to malformed inputs, injection vectors, and unexpected data shapes.
decision: Introduced `agent_core/security/tool_schema.py` using Pydantic models to validate all NLP tool arguments before execution. Invalid or non-conforming payloads are rejected prior to any tool invocation.
rationale: Pydantic provides declarative type coercion and constraint enforcement, guaranteeing that only well-formed, expected argument structures reach downstream tools. This shifts validation from runtime defensive checks inside each tool to a single upfront schema gate, improving reliability and security posture.

title: Self-modification guard to prevent agent tampering with its own security modules
context: No mechanism existed to detect or block the agent from modifying files within its own `agent_core/security/` directory, which could allow a compromised agent to disable containment, shell allowlists, schema validation, or sanitizers.
rationale: Protecting security-critical source paths is essential for defense-in-depth: if an attacker can alter the guardrails themselves, all other protections become meaningless. This guard acts as a final barrier ensuring the integrity of the enforcement layer cannot be subverted from within.

title: Add DuckDuckGo web search as an NLP tool
context: The analysis asks for DuckDuckGo web search to be added to agent.py, reused from ReactAgent, and integrated into the NLP tool loop.
decision: Add a web_search tool schema and handler so natural-language prompts can invoke DuckDuckGo search through the existing NLP tool loop.
rationale: This is the core requested capability and fits the existing ToolLoopRunner and NLP tool pattern.

title: Define the web_search tool contract
context: The analysis identifies missing details for exact tool name, arguments, output format, max_results, allowed domains, and rate-limit/offline behavior.
decision: Define the tool name, accepted arguments, return shape, truncation limits, allowed domains, and failure behavior for web_search.
rationale: A clear contract is needed for the NLP schema, handler, tests, and predictable model behavior.

title: Treat web search results as untrusted input
context: The threat model identifies prompt injection via search results and notes that web content can steer later tool calls.
decision: Wrap all web search results as untrusted data and prevent automatic execution of sensitive tools based solely on web content.
rationale: External web content is a prompt-injection vector and must not be treated as trusted instructions.

title: Decide whether web_search may fetch URLs
context: The scope says no arbitrary URL fetch unless specified, and the analysis lists URL follow-up as an open question.
decision: Decide whether web_search returns snippets only or also fetches page content; if URL fetch is allowed, require URL validation, domain allowlisting, and SSRF protections.
rationale: URL fetch expands the attack surface through SSRF, exfiltration, and possible authenticated actions.

title: Standardize on one LLM provider abstraction
context: The analysis identifies three conflicting provider abstractions: LLMProvider Protocol, AsyncLLMProvider ABC with registry, and a separate httpx LLMClient, while the spec requires supporting providers other than LM Studio.
decision: Choose one canonical provider abstraction, likely the LLMProvider Protocol, and bridge or deprecate the other two.
rationale: A single contract prevents duplicated behavior, config loss, and tool-loop breakage when adding providers.

title: Introduce configured provider factory or registry
context: LLMClient hardcodes LMStudioProvider and the existing registry may create default instances without passing provider config.
decision: Implement a factory or registry that accepts provider name and settings such as base_url, api_key, and model, then returns a configured provider instance.
rationale: Enables runtime provider selection without hardcoding and avoids silently dropping provider configuration.

title: Keep LM Studio as default provider
context: The scope requires keeping LM Studio functional while adding other providers, and the analysis assumes LM Studio remains default when nothing is configured.
decision: Default to LM Studio when no provider is explicitly configured.
rationale: Preserves backward compatibility and a local fallback for existing users.

title: Make model resolution provider-aware
context: resolve_model and KNOWN_MODELS are described as LM Studio specific, and the model REPL command manages models via the LM Studio API.
decision: Replace LM Studio-specific model resolution with provider-aware model discovery, defaults, and validation.
rationale: Other providers cannot rely on LM Studio model endpoints or model lists.

title: Normalize provider-specific payload construction
context: LMStudioProvider._build_payload sends LM Studio-only knobs for disable_thinking, which other providers may reject or ignore.
decision: Move provider-specific payload logic into each provider implementation and keep the shared contract minimal.
rationale: Prevents 400 errors and behavior drift when the same tool loop runs against different providers.

title: Make model profiles and prompt cache provider-aware
context: model_profiles.py, prompt_cache.py, metrics_tracker.py, and meta_policy.py may assume LM Studio-specific profiles or lack a provider dimension.
decision: Update model profiles, prompt templates, and performance tracking to include provider-specific variants or fallbacks.
rationale: Different providers may require different prompt formats, model profiles, or performance baselines.

title: Construct a dedicated harnessfix sub-package
context: Scope says to build a new harnessfix/ sub-package covering tracing, HTIR, links, diagnose, repairs, and loop/reader, and to instrument ToolLoopRunner.run().
decision: Create harnessfix/ with tracing, HTIR, link, diagnose, repairs/, and loop/reader modules; expose it as python -m harnessfix.loop.
rationale: Keeps all new code in one prefix, avoids scattering instrumentation, and makes the closed loop runnable as a module.

title: Restrict repair scope to the harness layer
context: Boundaries state no model changes, no prompt-tuning-as-primary-lever, and no security-policy changes without trace evidence.
decision: Limit changes to harness/tool-loop behavior; prohibit model changes and prompt-tuning as the primary lever; require trace evidence for security-policy changes.
rationale: Prevents the repair loop from silently altering model behavior or security enforcement, preserving benchmark meaning.

title: Require a human review gate before merging repairs
context: Threat model and boundaries say no auto-merge without a human review gate, while the loop section describes automated accept/reject.
decision: Add an explicit human approval step before any accepted repair is merged; decide whether it fires per-repair or after the summary batch.
rationale: A fully automated loop could accept subtle security regressions; human oversight is required to catch what tests miss.

title: Enforce mypy strict and ≤150 lines per file
context: Scope says all new code under the harnessfix/ prefix must be ≤150 lines/file and pass mypy strict.
decision: Keep every new file under 150 lines and run mypy strict on the harnessfix package.
rationale: Limits module size and typing rigor to make the repair loop auditable and less error-prone.

title: Use Pydantic v2 for HTIR models
context: Dependencies say Pydantic v2, already present in tool_router.py, is to be used for HTIR models.
decision: Define HTIR trace and graph models with Pydantic v2.
rationale: Leverages an existing dependency, provides schema validation for untrusted traces, and reduces new dependencies.

title: Select a single canonical CorrelationIdContext
context: Risk: both agent_core/context_management.py and logging_config.py define CorrelationIdContext with different defaults; the tracer must not add a third.
decision: Make agent_core/context_management.py the canonical source and adapt logging_config.py to use it, or explicitly prefer one for tracing.
rationale: Avoids conflicting defaults and ensures every trace event can share one correlation ID source.

title: Define 'execution environment' facet around shell execution
context: Assumptions interpret 'execution environment' as the subprocess/shell execution paths in agent.py _execute_tool_call and tool_router.py ShellCommandHandler.
decision: Map the execution-environment facet to the shell/subprocess code paths in _execute_tool_call and ShellCommandHandler.
rationale: Gives the facet a concrete, discoverable implementation and enables future heuristic signatures.

title: Treat guard-note strings in tool_loop.py as trusted static text
context: Diagnosis matches on _DEADLINE_NOTE / _STUCK_SYNTHESIS_NOTE; a lifecycle repair changing those strings silently disables diagnosis.
decision: Mark guard-note strings as immutable/trusted during repair runs and protect them in repair whitelists; all non-guard trace-derived text is untrusted.
rationale: Keeps diagnosis signatures stable and prevents repairs from accidentally blinding the diagnostic tier.

title: Sanitize tool results before any LLM consumption
context: Threat model: _execute_tool_call returns raw file contents and stdout/stderr into traces, enabling prompt injection via tool results.
decision: Pass all tool results through Sanitizer.sanitize_and_mask before storing in traces or sending to the LLM diagnostic tier.
rationale: Treats tool output as untrusted and prevents poisoned workspace files from steering repairs or reviewer agents.

title: Schema-validate and size-limit parsed trace files
context: Risk: reports/traces/*.jsonl is re-parsed by harnessfix/reader.py; forged traces could steer diagnosis.
decision: Implement schema validation and maximum size limits in harnessfix/reader.py for all trace JSONL inputs.
rationale: Prevents trace-file poisoning and malformed data from corrupting diagnosis or the repair loop.

title: Make the acceptance gate and benchmark scorers immutable during a repair run
context: Risk of self-referential verification: if the loop can modify benchmark.py scorers, 'pass rate improves' is trivially hackable.
decision: Hash-verify and exclude benchmark.py answering/scoring functions and the loop's acceptance gates from the repairable set.
rationale: Prevents reward hacking by ensuring pass-rate improvements are measured against a fixed, trusted evaluator.

title: Create a repair-target whitelist and forbid high-risk paths
context: Threat model lists off-limits files/dirs: harnessfix/ itself, benchmark.py scorers, _blocked_shell_command, and agent_core/security allowlists.
decision: Define an explicit whitelist of files the repair loop may change; forbid repairs to the acceptance gate, benchmark scoring, security enforcement, and the harnessfix package itself.
rationale: Contains capability escalation and prevents the loop from weakening sandbox or gate logic.

title: Use git-revertible standalone commits for repairs
context: Success/recovery says each repair is standalone and git-revertible; the loop restores workspace to clean state between iterations.
decision: Make harnessfix.loop create one git-revertible commit per repair and reset the workspace between iterations.
rationale: Makes rejection trivial, preserves audit trail, and avoids accumulated uncommitted changes.

title: Attach correlation ID and layer facet to every trace event
context: Audit trail says every trace event carries correlation ID + layer facet; diagnoses cite HTIR link IDs.
decision: Require the tracer to stamp each event with the canonical correlation ID and one of the seven layer facets, and require diagnoses to reference HTIR link IDs.
rationale: Enables end-to-end auditability and maps failures to taxonomy facets.

title: Use pass-rate gain and zero-regression as acceptance criteria
context: Success metrics require 0 regressions in pytest + security benchmarks and ≥1pt pass-rate gain to accept a repair.
decision: Accept a repair only if the full pytest suite and security benchmarks have zero regressions and the benchmark pass rate improves by at least 1 percentage point.
rationale: Establishes a safe, measurable bar for harness repairs and prevents overfitting to one trace.

title: Decide how the closed loop exercises the tool-loop harness
context: Risk: benchmark.py query_model makes single-shot urllib calls and never invokes ToolLoopRunner; as specced, harness repairs cannot change benchmark pass rate.
decision: Choose and implement either a new agentic benchmark routed through ToolLoopRunner or a harness-routed mode of benchmark.py with byte-identical --no-trace behavior.
rationale: The closed-loop acceptance metrics are only meaningful if repairs measurably affect a harness-exercising benchmark.

title: Define the task_id unit for trace files
context: Missing info: ToolLoopRunner.run() has no task_id, chat_nlp chains up to _MAX_CHAINED_RUNS = 6, benchmark uses question_idx; unclear unit for reports/traces/{task_id}.jsonl.
decision: Decide whether a trace file maps to one run() invocation, one chat_nlp turn including chained sub-runs, one benchmark question, or a new explicit task_id parameter on run().
rationale: Trace granularity affects diagnosis scope and the ability to correlate repairs with benchmark outcomes.

title: Establish the precision metric and labeled set for LLM-tier activation
context: Missing info: 'LLM tier must not run unless heuristic precision < 70%' has no denominator or labeled gold set.
decision: Choose a labeled gold set of historical failed traces or bootstrap labels from first-round repair acceptances; define heuristic precision as an agreed metric before enabling the LLM tier.
rationale: Without a denominator the <70% gate is vacuous and the LLM tier could run prematurely.

title: Place the human review gate at a defined point in the loop
context: Clarifying question: does the gate pause after each accepted repair or review the whole repair set after summary.json; behavior in headless/CI is also unspecified.
decision: Define whether approval is per-repair or post-batch and specify headless/CI behavior, such as fail-closed if no human approver is available.
rationale: Resolves conflicting specs and ensures no auto-merge occurs without explicit human approval.

title: Choose repair application and rollback mechanics
context: Missing info: how repairs are applied (AST patch, unified diff, or manual commit) and how failed/accepted repairs are rolled back cleanly between loop iterations.
decision: Specify whether repair generation emits AST patches, unified diffs, or manual commits; implement matching rollback in harnessfix.loop.
rationale: Determines how the loop can cleanly revert and re-run, and is required for reproducible iterations.

title: Create reports directories and add them to .gitignore
context: Dependencies say reports/traces/ and reports/harnessfix/ must be created and presumably git-ignored.
decision: Ensure reports/traces/ and reports/harnessfix/ exist at runtime and add them to .gitignore.
rationale: Keeps generated artifacts out of version control while preserving the required output paths.

title: Add payload-invariance and trace-completeness automated tests
context: Safety metrics require byte-identical LLM request payloads with tracing on vs --no-trace, every loop_end event present, every guard firing recorded, and no unsanitized tool results reaching LLM tiers.
decision: Implement automated tests asserting payload invariance, trace completeness, guard_triggered records, and absence of unsanitized tool content in traces/LLM input.
rationale: Makes safety properties verifiable in CI and catches regressions in the tracing layer.

title: Consolidate duplicate LLMClient and logging configs
context: Duplicate `LLMClient` definitions (agent.py, agent_core/llm_client.py) and two diverging `logging_config` modules create drift risk; three overlapping LLM client abstractions and duplicate CorrelationIdContext make module boundaries unclear.
decision: Create one shared LLM client abstraction and one logging configuration/correlation-context module to be used across all components.
rationale: Eliminates duplicated code, prevents drift, and clarifies module boundaries.

title: Workspace containment enforcement via path normalization
context: Path utilities needed to prevent directory traversal attacks. Alternatives: (a) block-listing specific patterns like `..` and absolute paths, (b) allow-listing only known-safe relative paths within workspace, (c) full canonicalization with symlink resolution plus boundary check.
decision: Chose full canonicalization approach — resolve symlinks and normalize paths then verify the resolved path remains within the designated workspace root before any file operation proceeds.
rationale: Canonicalization is robust against indirect traversal via symlinks or encoded sequences that block-lists would miss. It provides a single source of truth for containment rather than maintaining fragile pattern lists, aligning with defense-in-depth principles where every filesystem access validates boundaries post-resolution.

title: Allow-list validation with shell metacharacter rejection for command safety
context: Shell operation allow-list previously only block-listed known-dangerous patterns. Alternatives: (a) continue refining the block-list of regex patterns, (b) switch to structural parsing/tokenization rejecting any token containing shell metacharacters, pipes, redirection operators, or command chaining syntax, (c) sandbox execution in restricted subprocess with seccomp/capabilities.
decision: Adopted structural tokenization approach — parse input into tokens and reject commands where any token contains shell metacharacters (`;`, `|`, `&`, `>`, `<`, backticks, `$()`, etc.) rather than relying on pattern matching alone.
rationale: Block-lists are inherently incomplete against novel injection vectors; structural rejection of all metacharacters eliminates entire classes of chained-command and redirection attacks. This shifts validation from 'deny known bad' to 'permit only safe structure', reducing false negatives while keeping legitimate single-command execution viable.

title: Secret-manager utility backed by OS keyring with encrypted file fallback replacing plaintext .env
context: Secrets were stored in plaintext `.env` files. Alternatives: (a) keep plaintext env files but add gitignore rules, (b) use a dedicated secrets manager service (e.g., HashiCorp Vault), (c) local OS keyring API with encrypted-on-disk fallback for portability.
decision: Implemented local secret-manager utility using the OS-native keyring API as primary store, with an AES-encrypted file fallback when no system keyring is available.
rationale: OS keyring provides hardware/TEE-backed protection on supported platforms without external service dependencies. Encrypted-file fallback ensures functionality across headless/CI environments where keyring daemons are absent, balancing security and portability. This removes plaintext secrets from the repository entirely while avoiding infrastructure overhead of a networked vault.

title: Command registry pattern with explicit subcommand registration replacing ad-hoc dispatch
context: Agent commands were dispatched via loose function mapping. Alternatives: (a) maintain flat dict of command name to handler, (b) class-based command objects with metadata and validation hooks, (c) centralized registry with declarative registration decorators.
decision: Adopted a registry pattern in `agent_core/commands/registry.py` using decorator-based registration where each subcommand declares its schema, allowlist requirements, and execution entrypoint.
rationale: The registry provides a single authoritative list of available commands enabling discovery, help generation, and uniform pre-execution security checks (allowlist validation) before any handler runs. Declarative metadata co-located with handlers reduces drift between documentation and implementation, rejecting the implicit dispatch approach that hid command surfaces from static analysis.

title: Lint guard as pre-execution static analysis gate for generated code
context: Agent-generated code was written directly without validation. Alternatives: (a) execute and rely on runtime errors, (b) optional linting post-write, (c) mandatory lint pass before file write completes.
decision: Implemented `agent_core/utils/lint_guard.py` to run static analysis (syntax check + style rules) synchronously during the write command; writes are rejected if lint fails.
rationale: Pre-execution linting prevents syntactically broken or policy-violating code from entering the workspace, reducing downstream runtime failures and catching issues before they propagate through tool chains. Mandatory gating rejects post-hoc cleanup that would leave invalid artifacts in place during partial execution sequences.

title: Unified logging configuration with security-sensitive redaction policy
context: Logging was configured inconsistently across modules and could capture sensitive data. Alternatives: (a) per-module loggers with no filtering, (b) global filter redacting known secret patterns via regex, (c) structured logger with explicit allow-list of loggable fields and automatic scrubbing of paths/secrets.
decision: Consolidated logging into `agent_core/logging_config.py` using a structured logger that scrubs resolved secrets, normalized workspace-relative paths, and shell tokens before emission; only declared safe metadata fields are logged by default.
rationale: Structured redaction prevents accidental leakage of credentials or absolute filesystem locations in logs while preserving operational observability. Allow-listing loggable fields shifts from 'filter known bad' to 'emit known good', rejecting raw per-module logging that could expose secrets through unanticipated debug statements.

title: Decision record pattern for explicit architecture tradeoff documentation
context: Architectural choices were implicit in code without rationale capture. Alternatives: (a) inline comments only, (b) separate ADR documents outside codebase, (c) lightweight decision records embedded as structured entries within the agent core.
decision: Added `agent_core/decisions.py` maintaining a catalog of named decisions with context, chosen option, and rationale accessible at runtime for introspection and audit.
rationale: Embedding decisions in-code keeps tradeoff documentation co-located with implementation so reviewers see intent alongside behavior. Runtime accessibility enables agents to reference design rationale when explaining actions, rejecting scattered comments that fragment understanding across files.

title: Replace broad except Exception with specific exception types
context: Error handling in agent_core/agent.py had generic catch-all blocks at lines 86, 506, 570, 933. Alternatives: keep broad catches for simplicity, or use specific exceptions (ValueError, IOError, RuntimeError) with proper propagation.
decision: Adopted specific exception types and structured error propagation instead of blanket Exception catching.
rationale: Specific exceptions enable precise failure diagnosis, prevent masking unrelated bugs, allow callers to handle distinct error categories appropriately, and improve maintainability by making expected failure modes explicit.

title: Eliminate path resolution duplication in _execute_tool_call
context: _execute_tool_call duplicates path resolution logic (_resolve_nlp_path + to_windows_path + isdir check) already present in FileSystem.safe_path; run/git/diff tools reimplement subprocess patterns.
decision: Reuse agent_core/file_system.py safe_path and agent_core/subprocess_utils.py for all tool call path resolution and subprocess execution.
rationale: DRY compliance reduces maintenance burden and ensures consistent sandboxing across file ops, shell commands, git, and diff tools.

title: Unify path normalization across modules
context: agent.py uses to_windows_path() while agent_core/security/path_utils.py exposes an independent normalize_path() consumed by agent_core/tool_executor.py, agent_core/tools/file_ops.py, and agent_core/file_context_retriever.py; file_system.py and file_searcher.py carry their own normalize_path/_safe_path implementations - divergent behavior.
decision: Consolidate all path normalization into a single canonical implementation (agent_core/security/path_utils.py) and have agent.py, tool_router.py, file_system.py, and file_searcher.py delegate to it instead of maintaining separate implementations.
rationale: A single source of truth for workspace sandboxing prevents inconsistent security enforcement and reduces DRY violations across the current implementations.

title: Sanitize shell commands and file contents before trace persistence to prevent secret leakage
context: The risks section flagged over-collection/PII: shell commands and full file contents may leak secrets into traces. The analysis cited `agent_core/security/sanitizer.py` and a phantom `agent_core/security/secrets.py` masker.
decision: Route all trace-bound shell strings and file content through the verified `agent_core/security/sanitizer.py`, with secret masking via the real `agent_core/security/secrets.py` (confirmed present in workspace listing), before persistence via `harnessfix.tracing.TraceWriter`.
rationale: Sanitization must reference modules that actually exist; both sanitizer and secrets modules are in the ground-truth listing.

title: Make instrumentation invisible unless tracing is enabled (opt-out via AGENT_NO_TRACE=1)
context: The dependencies section noted `benchmarks/security_benchmarks.py` and existing tests assert on stdout/history, not traces; instrumentation must be invisible unless tracing enabled. Traces are opt-out per `conftest.py`.
decision: Gate all file-affected recording behind the verified trace infrastructure (`harnessfix.tracing.TraceWriter`, imported in agent.py) with opt-out via `AGENT_NO_TRACE=1` so benchmarks and tests asserting on stdout/history remain unaffected.
rationale: Invisible instrumentation preserves existing test contracts; the trace infra is confirmed present in both `agent.py` imports and `harnessfix/tracing.py`.

title: Record files affected by each traced tool call in tool_result/tool_error trace events
context: The original self-improvement goal (files-affected recording per tool/nlp) had analysis but no implementation. ToolLoopRunner already emits trace events and supports decision #048 invisibility, but events carried no file-level effects, so trace consumers could not audit what the agent touched.
decision: Add effects_fn (tool_name, args) -> [paths] to ToolLoopRunner (init + run); the loop attaches affected_files to tool_result and tool_error events, invoking the callback only when a trace sink exists and never raising. Agent wires _take_trace_effects into chat_nlp per run, arming a _pending_effects buffer only while a TraceWriter exists (decision #048) and recording read/write/edit/fix targets in _execute_tool_call via _note_effect (abspath-normalized, deduplicated).
rationale: Loop-level attachment keeps the trace schema uniform and works for any runner embedding; the None-when-untraced buffer keeps untraced runs byte-identical (verified by tests and full suite). REPL registry commands are not yet instrumented - separate increment.

title: Stamp traces with model/profile metadata and record the user prompt as the first event
context: Trace corpus analysis showed traces carried no prompt, model name, or profile, and correlation_id was empty everywhere. The verification gate cannot attribute failures to model+profile context without it.
decision: TraceWriter gains a meta dict (model, profile) stamped onto EVERY record via {**self._meta, **event}; agent.py chat_nlp wraps the tool-call loop in CorrelationIdContext and constructs the writer with meta={model: self.model_name, profile: getattr(self.llm, "_profile_name", None)}; a new KIND_TASK_BEGIN event (emit_task_begin) records the user input, truncated to PROMPT_CAP=500. Dashboard renders prompt/model/profile and the aggregated affected_files per task.
rationale: Meta stamping at the writer boundary keeps the emitter (tool_loop) schema-agnostic; per-turn correlation ids via contextvar survive the async loop; old traces degrade gracefully (empty columns) in the dashboard.

title: String-collision guard must exclude the guard's own fixture tests
context: The repair loop was self-blocked: the only real repair (tool-interface-error-detail, fragment "Tool error: ") collided with its own guard tests (test_harnessfix_collisions.py, test_harnessfix_loop.py) which contain the fragment as a literal. Verdict was permanently skipped_test_collision.
decision: find_test_collisions gains exclude_files (default GUARD_TEST_FILENAMES = the two guard test files). The loop scans once without exclusion, splits hits into guard-test hits (recorded as ignored_guard_test_hits) vs real pinning tests (still blocking). Guard tests are updated alongside any repair, so they never pin the OLD runtime string.
rationale: A guard that blocks every repair is a dead loop; excluding fixtures whose content is exercise-literals, not pins, restores the gate while real assertion pins (e.g. test_tool_loop_nlp.py) still block.

title: Diagnose interrupted runs and task abandonment via trace shape and affected_files
context: Real corpus had traces with 300+ events and no loop_end that diagnose_corpus skipped entirely (not is_failed). Others mutated files then ended non-completed; diagnosis fell through to a crude stuck heuristic.
decision: has_loop_end() and affected_files() on TraceGraph; corpus counts any trace without loop_end and >= MIN_ACTIVITY_EVENTS (3) as failed; diagnose adds: abandonment signature (affected_files present + non-completed end or no loop_end, lifecycle 'task ended non-completed after mutating N file(s)'), explicit interrupted-run signature (no loop_end), and the stuck mechanism now names the repeating tool. Order: explicit tool errors > abandonment > stuck > interrupted > guards.
rationale: loop_end is ALWAYS written by the runner's finally, so a missing one is a crash/kill/provider loss, not a normal end; 1-2 event stubs (aborted demo writes) are filtered to avoid noise. Effect-aware abandonment is more specific than stuck heuristics and uses the #049 field.

title: Human verification gate: review command with labeling and diagnosis-pinning regression export
context: The loop produces verdicts and diagnoses, but nothing helped the human gate review WHY a task failed: no per-task prompt/model/effects/outcome view, no labeling, no way to pin a diagnosis against future changes.
decision: New harnessfix/review.py builds a per-task ReviewRecord ledger (prompt, model, profile, outcome, guards, affected_files, root_layer, mechanism) from traces + persisted diagnoses; REPL command 'review' (refresh/list/show/label/export) persists reports/harnessfix/review.json (gitignored) with dispositions bug|regression|noise|ok and exports labeled tasks as generated pytest pins (reports/harnessfix/generated) asserting the diagnosis layer and a mechanism substring.
rationale: Labels feed the improvement loop (which failure types dominate per model+profile); generated pins make diagnosis changes fail loudly at the gate instead of silently reclassifying reviewed tasks. Ledger stays human-owned, out of git.

title: Decide review: flag decisions whose affected_files no longer exist
context: The decision ledger is a living document; nothing checked whether recorded affected_files still exist on disk, so superseded decisions lingered silently as authoritative.
decision: agent_core/decisions.py gains find_stale_decisions (workspace, decisions) -> decisions annotated with _missing_files (non-mutating); decide review subcommand reports stale files per decision, open contradictions (status not resolved/superseded), and a tip line.
rationale: Stale references are candidates for verification or supersession; the human gate decides, the command only surfaces them.

title: Key benchmark results by model|profile and give reasoning models a real token budget
context: Benchmark results were keyed by model name only, though the same model under deep-analysis vs fast-codegen behaves differently. Worse, qwen3.8-27b (a reasoning model) burned the 512 max_tokens on reasoning_content and returned EMPTY content (finish_reason length), scoring False it did not deserve.
decision: ModelResult gains profile; results keyed model|profile everywhere (benchmark.py, reports/models.json, gates._benchmark_key); benchmark.py gets --profile and --max-tokens (default 2048) with the query raising the budget so reasoning finishes AND the answer exists; run_benchmark_gate accepts profile, passes it through, and parses the LIST-form --output file (was crashing on .get() of a list). Baseline recorded: qwen/qwen3.8-27b|deep-analysis = 84.7% overall (coding 93.3, avg latency 12.3s).
rationale: Like-with-like comparison is a precondition for the benchmark gate to mean anything; the empty-content bug made every reasoning-model score a lower bound. Verified: same question with 2048 tokens yields content with finish_reason stop.

title: scripts/audit_invariants.py: automated AGENTS.md invariant audit
context: Invariants (commit-after-session, paired memory files, phantom-module check, trace health) were memory-only; nothing enforced or reported them.
decision: Standalone audit script: git status --porcelain (WARN normally, ERROR with --strict), .decisions.json validity, agent_memory.json/chat_history.json both-or-neither, phantom modules named in latest .docs/<ts>/ docs but missing on disk, trace corpus interrupted-run ratio (decision #052) plus last loop verdict, backups/ existence. Exit 1 only on errors; warnings are informational.
rationale: A zero-dependency script the gate can invoke post-commit; keeps invariant enforcement in the repo rather than in the model's memory.

title: Replace ad hoc print-based diagnostics with structured logging
context: Analysis suggests agent.py uses print-based diagnostics and hardcoded warnings instead of structured logs, making incident diagnosis and correlation harder.
decision: Decide whether to route agent.py diagnostics through structured logging with correlation identifiers.
rationale: Enables production diagnosis and correlation.

title: Reconstruct deleted uncommitted agent_core/tests from pyc skeletons
context: The 2026-08-18 23:18 implement run wrote 5 files (agent_core/tests/__init__.py + 4 entry-point test modules) and compiled them, but they were never committed and were deleted before the next session. Git had no copies (never entered the object store); only __pycache__/*.pyc survived. Marshalled code objects (names, docstrings, constants) were extracted to recover the full test skeleton, then the tests were rewritten against the current codebase APIs.
decision: Keep the reconstructed tests as current-behavior pins (31 tests green). Where the planned API did not exist (LLMClient.complete, tool_router typed timeout), tests were adapted to the real APIs (LLMClient.chat, pydantic arg validation). The __pycache__ residue was kept as the only surviving artifact.
rationale: Uncommitted work is unrecoverable (invariant #4); this incident is the second data loss after the deleted agent.py. pyc extraction is the only recovery path when a file was compiled but never committed.

title: Test package initialization marker
context: Adding an __init__.py to the agent_core/tests directory to mark it as a Python package for test discovery and collection.
decision: Created an empty __init__.py file in the tests directory.
rationale: Enables pytest to properly discover and import test modules when running tests from the project root, ensuring consistent test collection behavior.

title: History-assisted implement/fix from past executions
context: implement and fix injected past decisions into prompts but never past tool results/errors, even though the trace corpus (69 traces, ~6000 events) and review ledger existed. A 2026-08-19 paste-session fix silently never took effect in the running REPL (stale in-memory modules), showing history is only useful if both recorded richly and consumed.
decision: Added harnessfix/history.py: a process-cached index over reports/traces/ plus a structured execution ledger reports/history/executions.jsonl (gitignored), with PAST EXECUTION NOTES formatters. implement injects per-batch history next to the decisions block (--no-history opt-out) and appends a structured run summary; fix injects per-file history in _fix_traceback and --desc modes and appends run summaries. search/list_files/analyze now record affected_files in traces (read/write/edit/fix already did).
rationale: Prompt-level history is purely additive read-only context and cannot affect implement write/cascade invariants (dependency cascade safety, wholesale-rewrite guard, batch-name checks). Matching handles old-format traces via args-path suffix (abs to rel) and new-format affected_files; directory args match only direct children to avoid workspace-wide noise. Recording affected_files for read-only tools plus structured run summaries makes future history precise.
